title: External tables, BigLake and querying without ingesting

videos.script: Quitanda's orders already live in a bucket, as Parquet files, one folder a day. {{bucket}} Loading them into BigQuery copies them, and then they are stored twice. {{twice}} An external table leaves them where they are. BigQuery reads the files at the moment a query runs. {{external}} You will do what its reader does. List the objects, skip the days the filter rules out, and fetch only the bytes of two columns. {{ranges}} Every file costs a footer and a few requests, and you will count them. {{count}} BigLake adds a connection, so analysts never touch the bucket, and a cache of what the files contain. {{biglake}} Object tables list pictures and receipts. Iceberg lets several engines change the same files safely. {{iceberg}} Then the bill. Cheaper storage at first, no long-term discount ever, and requests that grow with the number of files. {{cost}}
